Though Sha'ne and Char'li had escaped the horrors of The Burrows it would be three days until they were discovered by a passing caravan wandering through the forest starving and disorientated. The caravan as luck would have it had been on their way to the fledgling settlement of the Med'ja-Hom'te and so after a short an uneventful journey (of which they spent the majority sleeping) they were at last reunited with their kin.

The arrival of the two sickly looking Med'ja had been met with both rumor and surprise as the tribe had sent a contingent of warriors and diggers to the Burrows upon the clearing of the storm only to be repelled by an unknown force. For days the Shamans had studied the barrier attempting to find a way through however many of the tribesmen had begun to suffer from strange and violent nightmares ultimately retreating once the warriors temper and composure had worn down under the strain of the assault and they had begun to turn on one another.

Upon learning of their tale and the horrors beneath the surface the elders of the Med'ja-Hom'te sent yet another contingent to the Burrows believing that with the King felled they would be able to rescue their kin, however this was not to be. Arriving at the entrance the found the barrier had remained for though the poison had ravage his body, so strong was the King'swill that he had refused to die. With dark energies now his sole tie to the world of the living Ma'Ten dragged his broken body back to his throne, falling into a deep slumber, his dark powers dragging his kin down with him. Together they would lie in endless slumber, sustained by the King's magics until he once again awoke to command them.

*The Shaman's entrance was never found and so the Tribe mourned, their brothers and sisters lost to the darkness, consumed by the mad King's curse.* -----

Under the light of the sun and surrounded by their kin Sha'ne and Char'li were slowly filled with the joy and vitality that they had enjoyed prior to the sundering of the tribe and the God's wrath smiting their home. Free from the King's magics the stone that had grown upon Char'lis tail grew brittle and shattered leaving him with only what had remained flesh and the new name of "Stumptail" Sha'ne too had received a permanent mark upon her body, for so pure and white had her fur become that she too would gain a name in "Snowpelt" which would remain with her until the end of her days.

---

Years passed and as our heroes healed and grew so did the tribe; other races of the world once only spoken of in stories had now become common visitors to Med'jan city of vines now known as the "Grove of Hom"; Saen migrants from the north, small and shy, the mighty Shrykes who commanded the skies but loathed to enter beneath the vines boughs and the many more who sought the Southern Roost for trade.

The Shamans, having at last consolidated their collective knowledge returned to the tribe offering to share with them the writing handed down to them by the Gods, the first schools were created with many students later joining the Shamans at the Great tree not as members of the Brotherhood but as students of their lore, giving birth in a fashion to both the first Med'jan university and library.

It was on one such journey that Char'li, seeking to learn more about his own abilities, was introduced to the Flora who had come to reside within a great garden at the base of the tree, Thad'ja Songcaller having succeeded in leading them there some years prior. Though initially pleased that the mystery of the symbols had finally been solved they were less than excited at the revelation that the symbols the Pattern of the Gods the Flora had been decorating the Great Tree with were in fact merely the sides of a die, their combined work leading to little more than numerous floral arrangements and the creation of the primitive version of craps.

The Tribe was once again at peace, they had lost much and suffered great trials and emerged all the stronger, ready to face the world with loving hearts and an open mind just as their God had hoped for so long ago.

- END

Existing domains only

As you can see in the other thread we have several multiple and overlapping domains. We have 3 gods of rules ( order, law, justice) we have 3 gods of sun (flox, brightness, rhama) we have several gods of nature (zille, home, pome) several gods of chaos (chaos, entropy, slaanesh) etc.

We also have several gods claiming a multitude of domains.

If we allow the choosing of domains the same thing will happen:

  • People will drop in, pick up a big domain and not use it.
  • We will get players attempting to become the 5th god of sun cuzz they don't bother to check what's already a domain.

I think we covered a lot of domains in anarchy, so much so we have multiple gods of several domains. The choice this allows will be sufficient.

On domains

I vote Aye, with a restriction

Gods that only created a god are to lose their domain.

Those domains are available for claim.

With this restriction You can't ADD a domain to yourself, you can only SWAP domain.

  • Not Phyra: God of Order, Space, Chaos, Grass, Wind & Fire. (From a bunch of different gods)
  • Only Phyra: God of Sun. => Taken over from Ramza: God of Sun
  • OR Phyra: God of Pity, Sorrow, Compassion => Taken over from Dolor: God of Pity, Sorrow, Compassion

Only replacing/claiming of the originally chosen title.

Point 2

I'd like for those domains to be open to the current race/hero players as well, they might want to become a god? Or switch in an out at the sabbat? I see no reason why they should have restrictions I do not have.

On Opening the Pantheon

I've noticed that with the last Sabbath, many gods relinquished their control of a race to resume their godly duties. This being the case, right now there are far more players playing gods than there are playing races or hero characters.

That being said, what sort of balance would we like to see when it comes to the amount of players in the different positions, (Gods, Races, Heroes), and based off of that, should we open the Pantheon at all during this time?

For reference: There are 6 races being played that I'm aware of (Water Elementals, Candid, Med'ja, Spectrus Manius, Chlora, Saen) and probably over 12 gods being played, now that there's been a roll call.

Age of Ascension? Allow new players to claim a God. If they aren't active, have them relinquish it again. I think a swap is good, although I'm not interested in that. It's also a great way for newer players who missed the age of creation to have a shot at Godhood.

But the way things played out seem like real history. Some gods are just forgotten or not worshiped anymore. Look at the population of Norse believers today. It's negligable. Same for SavageGods. Some gods just lost worshipers or believers. It can be canon to lose gods.

Swapping domains (like people seem to be suggesting) doesn't seem especially bad, (Nice idea @Oveass ) I just have one concern. Gods ave historically been really defined by their domain. Their personality, their cares and motivations, their appearance, everything about a god has been largely defined by what they are god of. If Phyra, god of Order, becomes god of Sorrow and Compassion, is he to still be obsessed by the ordering of the universe? Does he use his new powers to achieve it in a new way, then a week later go back to Order? That feels weird to me, from a role-playing perspective.

Beyond that, yeah I think we could use some new gods or some old gods under new players. Let's face it, this game seems like it's most fun to play as a god, and my feeling is we mostly encourage races and heroes so that the gods have someone to lord over (and so have even more fun).

I personally am not too worried about major domains becoming picked up then quickly abandoned or anything, because a god of time is only lord of time if they are active - if this falls into disuse, well, we're all gods here, and without a god of time to tell us not to meddle with time, we can and will. A lot of us are not very motivated to, because see point 1 - we don't have much of an opinion on time. What's important is defined largely by 'is there a god of it,' it's not like any domains are more powerful than any other.That said, overlapping has been of an issue, and one of the core tenants upon founding was 'one god per thing,' so we could gently encourage people not to overlap too strongly.
I'd say open the pantheon since we have so few people. We already let people claim domains from gods who are Forgotten as an action I thought.

I am in favour of opening the Pantheon. While Oveass's concerns about the massive backlog of pure god spam that occurred at the infancy of this sub are justified, I doubt there will be a repeat of said events.

I feel that a good part of the joy of playing a god is the idea of playing a god that seems interesting to you, and the best way to do that is for a person to be given the choice to create and customize a god, as opposed to having to select between a small roster of pre-made deities. While there are a lot of pre-existing gods, some of them are downright silly. (God of Chicken Noodle Soup comes to mind.)

I feel that the massive amount of text and story that we put out is already a pretty daunting deterrent to casual people looking at the thread. Furthermore, allowing new domains and the shifting of a few domains allows the fleshing out or evolution of certain gods.

Evidently I doubt this will pass, seeing the support Oveass seems to have, but I do feel that there is something to be said for letting new god players create their own god, after all, the duty of the Gods in this game is mostly in creation and meddling. To have neither creation nor meddling in the God choosing process seems a little peculiar. Neither is it fair to set gods as being either static of having to take a total change in aspects.

As for overlapping domains, some degree of domain overlap can be expected, and in fact could be good. Different creators might have a different idea of what seemingly similar aspects can do, and therefore take similar aspects in different directions, showcasing the multi-faceted nature of the divine domains.

Anyways, just my two cents.
